text.p: Staburadze confectionery said on Tuesday it saw a better profit this year mainly due to increased volume more intensive work on the local market and increased export share.
"This year could definitely be better than 1996. Profit will be good," Staburadze president Ivar Rudzitis told Reuters in an interview.
He refused to give more balance sheet figures as the audit of 1996 results was currently underway so it will be ready before the shareholder meeting on April 29.
"We plan to to have production volume of 7,000 tonnes versus some 6,300 last year," Rudzitis said.
"In money terms, we will have turnover of 8 million lats, which to my mind is quite impressive for a confectionery firm," he added.
In 1996 Staburadze had some 7 million lats of turnover.
"Our plans are strictly based on more intensive work in the local market where we sell 90 percent of our produce," the Staburadze president said.
"Some 10 percent of our products, mainly biscuits and waffels, will be exported this year to Russia and a tiny fraction to Germany," he added.
"We are succesful in working with our competition but our biggest problem is low purchasing power and we are looking for exports to compesate this," Rudzitis said.
Some 60 percent of Staburadze produce is biscuits, the rest being waffels, cakes and marzipan.
